standard_prerequisites.name: The Hilbert function of a parameter ideal is a numerical polynomial of degree equal to the dimension
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the leading coefficient e_I/d! meaningful and fixes the degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of the monomial map onto the graded pieces I^n/I^{n+1}
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the length inequality between consecutive quotients.

standard_prerequisites.name: Comparison of leading coefficients of two numerical polynomials of the same degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the inequality between polynomials into the numerical bound on e_I.

core_obligations: Record that the function n -> length_R(R/I^{n+1}) is a numerical polynomial, by the Hilbert-function proposition, and that it has degree d, by the dimension proposition (proof lines 38270-38273).
Dispose of d = 0 as trivial and reduce d = 1 to the earlier one-dimensional lemma (proof lines 38274-38275).

Exhibit the surjection from the direct sum of copies of R/I indexed by tuples i_1, ..., i_d >= 0 with sum n onto I^n/I^{n+1}, sending the basis element for a tuple to the class of g_1^{i_1} ... g_d^{i_d} (proof lines 38276-38283).
Conclude the inequality length_R(R/I^{n+1}) - length_R(R/I^n) <= length_R(R/I) binom(n + d - 1, d - 1) (proof lines 38284-38288).

For d >= 2 compare leading coefficients: the left-hand numerical polynomial has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient e_I/(d-1)!, while the right-hand polynomial has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient length_R(R/I)/(d-1)!, whence e_I <= length_R(R/I) (proof lines 38289-38293).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension d, a system of parameters g_1, ..., g_d with I = (g_1, ..., g_d), and asserts that if e_I/d! is the leading coefficient of the numerical polynomial n -> length_R(R/I^{n+1}), then e_I <= length_R(R/I) (source lines 38260-38267). The proof first records the two structural inputs: the function is a numerical polynomial by the Hilbert-function proposition, and it has degree d by the dimension proposition (proof lines 38270-38273). It disposes of d = 0 as trivial and reduces d = 1 to the earlier one-dimensional statement (proof lines 38274-38275). The general case is the substantive computation. The proof exhibits the surjection from the direct sum of copies of R/I indexed by the tuples i_1, ..., i_d >= 0 with sum n, onto I^n/I^{n+1}, sending the basis element to the class of the monomial g_1^{i_1} ... g_d^{i_d} (proof lines 38276-38283). This yields the inequality length_R(R/I^{n+1}) - length_R(R/I^n) <= length_R(R/I) binom(n + d - 1, d - 1) (proof lines 38284-38288). The proof then compares leading coefficients: for d >= 2 the numerical polynomial on the left has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient e_I/(d-1)!, and the polynomial on the right has degree d - 1 with leading coefficient length_R(R/I)/(d-1)!, which gives the bound (proof lines 38289-38293). The non-routine content is the surjection onto the graded pieces of I^n with its binomial index count, and the leading-coefficient comparison.
